chunks: And what Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Fadalah from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Ibn 'Abbas was asked: 'Did the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) use perfume before visiting the House (Kaaba)?' He said: 'I saw the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) applying musk to his head before visiting the House.'

Therefore, in these two reports, it is not established that the permissibility of using perfume applies only upon completion of shaving the head before the visit, for the Mutamatti' or for the Hajj who is not a Mutamatti'.

And if that is not explicit in the two reports, we interpret them as applying to the Hajj who is not a Mutamatti', because it is permissible for him to use everything upon shaving his head, except women (i.e., prohibition of marrying women), only.
And the use of perfume is not permissible for the Mutamatti' along with that, unlike the others.
And that which indicates this is what he narrated:

key_terms.الزِّيَارَةِ: The visit to the Kaaba, often referring to Tawaf al-Ifadah.
key_terms.الطِّيبِ: Perfume/scent, prohibited for men in Ihram.
key_terms.الْحَاجِّ غَيْرِ الْمُتَمَتِّعِ: The pilgrim who performs Hajj and Umrah together or separately without the specific Mutamatti' structure.
key_terms.الْمُتَمَتِّعِ: The pilgrim who performs Umrah first, then Hajj, in the same season.
key_terms.حَلْقُ الرَّأْسِ: Shaving the head, a ritual act concluding Ihram.

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to use perfume during Hajj before shaving the head?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi employs the principle of *istishab* (presumption of continuity of permissibility) to argue that the Prophet’s use of musk before visiting the Kaaba indicates a general permission for the Hajj al-Qarin, whose restrictions are lifted entirely upon shaving. This contrasts with the Mutamatti', for whom perfume remains prohibited until the specific act of shaving concludes the major Ihram restrictions, highlighting the nuanced distinction between the two Hajj types in Shia fiqh. The analysis underscores how early reports from Ibn Abbas are interpreted to resolve apparent ambiguities in the timing of ritual prohibitions.
